meaningEn: Expressing respect toward the subject of the sentence.

notesEn.usage: Inserted into verb or adjective stems when the person performing the action is older, higher status, or deserving of high respect.
notesEn.nuance: Present polite form becomes ~(으)세요, past form becomes ~(으)셨어요.

notesId.formation: Kata Dasar berakhiran Vokal -> ~시~ / Kata Dasar berakhiran Konsonan -> ~으시~.
notesId.usage: Disisipkan pada kata dasar kata kerja atau kata sifat ketika orang yang melakukan tindakan lebih tua, memiliki status lebih tinggi, atau patut dihormati.
notesId.nuance: Bentuk sopan masa kini menjadi ~(으)세요, bentuk lampau menjadi ~(으)셨어요.

examples.meaningId: Ibu mau pergi ke mana sekarang?

quiz.question: What is the past honorific form of '가다' (to go)?
quiz.explanationId: 가다 + bentuk lampau honorifik ~(으)셨어요 menjadi 가셨어요.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: The teacher teaches Korean. -> 선생님께서 한국어를 가르치___요.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: Attach honorific polite present ending to stem 가르치.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: Tempelkan akhiran honorifik sopan masa kini pada kata dasar 가르치.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'The teacher teaches Korean.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Guru mengajar bahasa Korea.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use teacher (선생님께서) + Korean language (한국어를) + teach honorific (가르치세요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan guru (선생님께서) + bahasa Korea (한국어를) + mengajar honorifik (가르치세요).

meaningEn: Formal polite ending used in speeches, news, business, and military.
meaningId: Akhiran formal sopan yang digunakan dalam pidato, berita, bisnis, dan militer.

notesEn.formation: Vowel stem -> ~ㅂ니다 / Consonant stem -> ~습니다. Questions end in ~습니까 / ~ㅂ니까?
notesEn.usage: Used in formal situations, public presentations, or when speaking to groups/superiors in professional settings.
notesEn.nuance: More formal and strict than the standard polite style (~아/어요).

notesId.formation: Kata Dasar berakhiran Vokal -> ~ㅂ니다 / Kata Dasar berakhiran Konsonan -> ~습니다. Pertanyaan berakhiran ~습니까 / ~ㅂ니까?
notesId.usage: Digunakan dalam situasi formal, presentasi publik, atau saat berbicara kepada kelompok/atasan di lingkungan profesional.
notesId.nuance: Lebih formal dan kaku daripada bentuk sopan standar (~아/어요).

examples.meaningEn: Nice to meet you for the first time.
examples.meaningId: Senang berkenalan dengan Anda pertama kali.

examples.meaningEn: I will start the presentation now.

quiz.question: Which formal ending attaches to '갑니다' (go) from stem '가-'?
quiz.explanationEn: Since '가-' ends in a vowel, ~ㅂ니다 is added as a batchim to form 갑니다.
quiz.explanationId: Karena '가-' berakhiran vokal, ~ㅂ니다 ditambahkan sebagai batchim untuk membentuk 갑니다.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: Nice to meet you. -> 반갑습니다. -> 반갑___니다.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: Attach formal consonant suffix component to 반갑.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: Tempelkan komponen akhiran formal konsonan pada 반갑.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean (formal high): 'I will start the presentation now.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea (formal tingkat tinggi): 'Saya akan memulai presentasi sekarang.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use from now (지금부터) + presentation (발표를) + will start formal (시작하겠습니다).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan mulai sekarang (지금부터) + presentasi (발표를) + akan memulai formal (시작하겠습니다).

meaningEn: Expressing a reason or background fact ('you see / it's because').
meaningId: Mengekspresikan alasan atau fakta latar belakang ('sebab / tahu sendiri kan / karena').

notesEn.usage: Used to inform the listener of a reason or background fact they don't know yet, or to respond to a question politely.
notesEn.nuance: Gives a gentle 'you see, the reason is...' nuance.

notesId.usage: Digunakan untuk memberi tahu pendengar alasan atau fakta latar belakang yang belum mereka ketahui, atau merespons pertanyaan secara sopan.
notesId.nuance: Memberikan nuansa lembut 'karena begini, tahu...' atau 'asal kamu tahu...'

examples.meaningEn: Because I'm a bit busy right now, you see.
It's because I couldn't sleep yesterday, so I'm tired.
examples.meaningId: Soalnya kemarin saya tidak bisa tidur, jadi saya lelah.

examples.meaningEn: You see, I can't eat spicy food.
examples.meaningId: Soalnya saya tidak bisa makan makanan pedas.

quiz.question: What nuance does '~거든(요)' add at the end of a sentence?
quiz.explanationEn: ~거든(요) is used to state a reason or context that the listener might not be aware of.
quiz.explanationId: ~거든(요) digunakan untuk menyatakan alasan atau konteks yang mungkin belum diketahui pendengar.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: Because I'm a bit busy right now, you see. -> 제가 지금 좀 바쁘___요.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: Attach background reason ending before polite particle 요.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: Tempelkan akhiran alasan latar belakang sebelum partikel sopan 요.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'Because I'm a bit busy right now, you see.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Soalnya saya agak sibuk sekarang.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use I (제가) + now (지금) + a bit (좀) + busy reason (바쁘거든요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan saya (제가) + sekarang (지금) + agak (좀) + alasan sibuk (바쁘거든요).

pattern: Verb/Adj Stem + ~잖아(요) (Confirmation 'As you know / Isn't it?')
meaningEn: Reminding the listener of a shared fact ('as you know / isn't it?').
meaningId: Mengingatkan pendengar tentang fakta yang sudah diketahui bersama ('kan / bukankah...').

notesEn.usage: Used when arguing, correcting, or gently reminding the listener of something they already know or should know.
notesEn.nuance: Can sound defensive or soft depending on intonation.

notesId.formation: Kata Dasar Kata Kerja/Sifat + ~잖아(요). Lampau: ~았/었잖아(요). Kata Benda: ~(이)잖아(요).
notesId.usage: Digunakan saat berargumen, mengoreksi, atau mengingatkan pendengar secara lembut tentang sesuatu yang sudah mereka ketahui atau seharusnya ketahui.
notesId.nuance: Dapat terdengar membela diri atau ramah tergantung intonasi.

examples.meaningEn: Tomorrow is the weekend, as you know.
I told you already, didn't I?
This clothing is too expensive, as you can see.

quiz.question: When do you use '~잖아(요)'?
options: When reminding someone of a known fact
quiz.explanationEn: ~잖아(요) is used to state a fact that both speaker and listener know or should know.
quiz.explanationId: ~잖아(요) digunakan untuk menyatakan fakta yang sudah diketahui atau seharusnya diketahui oleh pembicara dan pendengar.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: Tomorrow is the weekend, as you know. -> 내일은 주말이___.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: Attach shared fact reminder suffix after noun+copula 주말이.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: Tempelkan akhiran pengingat fakta bersama setelah kata benda+kopula 주말이.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'Tomorrow is the weekend, as you know.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Besok kan akhir pekan.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use tomorrow (내일은) + weekend (주말) + shared fact ending (이잖아요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan besok (내일은) + akhir pekan (주말) + akhiran fakta bersama (이잖아요).

pattern: Verb/Adj Stem + ~(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 (No Way / It Can't Be)
meaningEn: Strong disbelief or conviction that something is impossible ('there is no way / it can't be').
meaningId: Ketidakpercayaan atau keyakinan kuat bahwa sesuatu tidak mungkin terjadi ('tidak mungkin / mustahil').

notesEn.formation: Vowel stem -> ~ㄹ 리가 없다 / Consonant stem -> ~을 리가 없다. Past: ~았/었을 리가 없다.
notesEn.usage: Used to strongly deny a possibility based on logical reasoning or knowledge.
notesEn.nuance: Can be turned into a rhetorical question: ~(으)ㄹ 리가 있어요? (Is there any way that...?).

notesId.formation: Kata Dasar berakhiran Vokal -> ~ㄹ 리가 없다 / Kata Dasar berakhiran Konsonan -> ~을 리가 없다. Lampau: ~았/었을 리가 없다.
notesId.usage: Digunakan untuk membantah kemungkinan secara kuat berdasarkan penalaran logis atau pengetahuan.
notesId.nuance: Dapat diubah menjadi pertanyaan retoris: ~(으)ㄹ 리가 있어요? (Mungkinkah...?).

examples.meaningEn: There is no way that rumor/statement is true.

examples.hangul: 민수 씨가 거짓말을 했을 리가 없어요.
examples.romaja: min-su ssi-ga geo-jit-mal-eul haes-seul li-ga eobs-eo-yo.
examples.meaningEn: There is no way Minsu lied.
There's no way it's finished already.
examples.meaningId: Tidak mungkin sudah selesai begitu cepat.

quiz.question: Which phrase expresses 'There is no way that is true'?
quiz.explanationEn: ~(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 expresses total disbelief or impossibility.
quiz.explanationId: ~(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 mengekspresikan ketidakpercayaan total atau ketidakmungkinan.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: There is no way that is true. -> 그 말이 사실일 ___ 없어요.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: Insert noun meaning 'reason/possibility' after fact future modifier 사실일.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: Masukan kata benda yang berarti 'alasan/kemungkinan' setelah penjelas masa depan 사실일.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'There is no way that statement is true.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Tidak mungkin perkataan itu benar.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use that word/statement (그 말이) + to be true modifier (사실일) + no way (리가 없어요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan perkataan itu (그 말이) + penjelas benar (사실일) + tidak mungkin (리가 없어요).
